# fetchaller

> MCP server that fetches any URL as clean markdown. No domain restrictions. Built-in web search, Reddit, tech-careers job search (Google, Microsoft, Apple, Meta, Amazon, Netflix, Uber, Oracle, PayPal, Adobe, NVIDIA, Salesforce, Cisco and any Workday, Eightfold or Oracle Recruiting board), marketplace, real-estate (realtor.ca), AliExpress, and Alibaba tools. Bot protection bypass is automatic.

## Tools

### fetch(url, maxTokens?, timeout?, raw?, method?, headers?, body?)

Fetch any URL and return clean markdown. Handles HTML, JSON, XML, CSV, PDF, SVG (raw), and binary images (returns metadata summary: type, filename, size, dimensions, Last-Modified, ETag). Normal Reddit URLs use compact structured New Reddit rendering (logged-out JSON plus the canonical wiki-tree SSR and, after a missing tree or exact unstructured anonymous 403, New Reddit's own logged-out `WikiPageRevisionsV2` page tree on the fixed `/svc/shreddit/graphql` route — no OAuth scope and no browser) with post score/upvote ratio, nested comments, links, rich media/polls, public state labels, and comment-permalink context; explicit `.json` remains raw and `raw=true` returns canonical New Reddit HTML. Site-specific cleanup for 20+ sites (GitHub, Reddit, Amazon, eBay, Stack Overflow, HN, Wikipedia, Medium, Hugging Face, DigiKey, Mouser, Molex, FCC (fcc.report, fcc.gov), Craigslist, Kijiji, realtor.ca (home search + individual listings with similar-listing reconstruction), aartech.ca (category/manufacturer/search listings and product pages, both priced from the site's own data since its HTML ships no prices), ui.com (UniFi store product and category pages, techspecs.ui.com, and installation guides — the store's HTML has the price but none of the technical specifications, which are read from the page's own data instead), Facebook Marketplace, Alibaba, AliExpress, RedFlagDeals, forums, TI, Soylent, vacuumwars.com incl. compare.vacuumwars.com and robotvacs.com (the robot-vacuum comparison tool, whose whole lab dataset -- every model's Vacuum Wars test scores and specs -- is read from the page's own data because the tool itself renders client-side and otherwise returns an empty board; comparison reads go to the tool's own uncached host rather than the cached copy, and say so; lab-tested and listed-only models are counted and ranked separately), Ashby (board index read from the public posting API, or from the hosted board's own GraphQL when an org has switched that API off, so a live board is never reported as empty) + Greenhouse + Lever + Gem + Dayforce + Cornerstone (CSOD) + Workday + BambooHR + JazzHR + HubSpot + Work at a Startup (YC) + wellfound.com (startup job search, job detail, company pages) job boards, plus the big-tech career boards (Eightfold tenants incl. Microsoft/Netflix/PayPal, amazon.jobs with inline pay bands, jobs.apple.com, metacareers.com, jobs.uber.com), plus embed/white-label detection for Ashby/BambooHR/JazzHR widgets and white-label Dayforce candidate portals on company-owned domains). All other sites get universal junk removal.

Reddit context behavior: request size and nesting scale with the caller's token budget. Rendering preserves whole sections and uses explicit omission markers and continuation links; compactness never silently removes public content.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| url | string | required | URL to fetch |
| maxTokens | integer | 25000 | Max tokens to return |
| timeout | integer | 10 | Request timeout in seconds |
| raw | boolean | false | Return raw HTML instead of markdown |
| method | string | GET | `GET` or `POST` |
| headers | object | — | Extra request headers (max 32; connection/framing headers refused) |
| body | string | — | Request body, POST only (max 1MB; Content-Type defaults to application/json for JSON bodies) |

POST reaches search and listing APIs that answer to nothing else — Getro (a
large share of VC portfolio job boards), Algolia, GraphQL gateways — whose
boards look static and read as empty over GET. A POST skips site-specific
handling and the response cache. `PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` are not accepted.

Two signals guard against silently wrong conclusions on JavaScript-rendered
pages: a `possibly_js_rendered` warning when a page's content is assembled in
the browser (so an un-hydrated shell is not read as an empty site), and
preservation of careers/jobs links from otherwise-stripped nav/header/footer.
A flagged shell also returns what it still declares — meta description,
canonical URL, and Organization `sameAs` profiles — which on a page that renders
to nothing is the whole usable answer.

### search(query, page?)

Web search via Google + DuckDuckGo. Returns titles, URLs, and snippets. Use `fetch` to read full pages from results.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| query | string | required | Search query |
| page | integer | 1 | Result page (1-indexed) |

### browse_reddit(subreddit, sort?, time?, limit?, after?, timeout?)

Browse subreddit posts. Returns Reddit's public score and upvote ratio (when returned), comment count, preview, pagination cursor, and canonical New Reddit URLs. Use `fetch` to read full post content and nested comments.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| subreddit | string | required | Subreddit name without r/ prefix |
| sort | string | hot | hot, new, top, rising |
| time | string | day | hour, day, week, month, year, all (for "top" sort only) |
| limit | integer | 10 | Number of posts (1-25) |
| after | string | — | Pagination cursor from previous response |
| timeout | integer | 10 | Request timeout in seconds |

### search_reddit(query, subreddit?, sort?, time?, limit?, after?, timeout?)

Search Reddit posts. Returns Reddit's public score and upvote ratio (when returned), comment count, preview, pagination cursor, and canonical New Reddit URLs. Use `fetch` to read full post content and nested comments.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| query | string | required | Search query |
| subreddit | string | — | Limit to subreddit (without r/) |
| sort | string | relevance | relevance, hot, top, new, comments |
| time | string | all | hour, day, week, month, year, all |
| limit | integer | 10 | Number of results (1-25) |
| after | string | — | Pagination cursor from previous response |
| timeout | integer | 10 | Request timeout in seconds |

### search_marketplace(query, location, platforms?, category?, sort?, condition?, min_price?, max_price?)

Search Kijiji, Craigslist, and Facebook Marketplace simultaneously. Returns grouped results. Use `fetch` on result URLs for full listing details.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| query | string | required | Search keywords |
| location | string | required | City name, optionally with province/state (e.g. "toronto", "st catharines, ON", "seattle") |
| platforms | string[] | all | kijiji, craigslist, facebook. Kijiji is Canada-only and auto-skipped for US locations. |
| category | string | all | all, cars, electronics, furniture, clothing, tools, free, bikes, phones, motorcycles, boats, rvs, auto_parts, sporting, toys, baby |
| sort | string | date | date, price_asc, price_desc, relevance |
| condition | string | — | new, like_new, good, fair |
| min_price | integer | — | Minimum price in dollars |
| max_price | integer | — | Maximum price in dollars |

### search_linkedin_jobs(keywords, location?, strict_location?, date_posted?, workplace?, experience?, job_type?, min_salary?, easy_apply?, under_10_applicants?, sort?, start?, limit?)

Search LinkedIn's public logged-out job board — no account required. Filters: date posted (any/24h/week/month), workplace (on_site/remote/hybrid), experience (internship..executive), job type (full_time/part_time/contract/temporary/internship), minimum salary (40k-120k), easy_apply (LinkedIn-internal application), under_10_applicants (few applicants so far). `strict_location` defaults to `true`: when `location` is supplied, each posting's own location must match; set it to `false` only when LinkedIn's broader geographic ranking is wanted. Returns title, company, location, posting date, LinkedIn's "Be an early applicant"/"Actively Hiring" badges when present, and a stable linkedin.com/jobs/view URL. Pagination via `start` (rows 0-999, 10 per page). `sort=recent` is applied client-side because LinkedIn's own sortBy is not honoured on this endpoint; salary is not published in logged-out results and is never implied.

### get_linkedin_job(job_id)

Full public detail for one LinkedIn posting: description, seniority level, employment type, job function, industries, applicant count. Applying requires a LinkedIn account. `fetch()` on a linkedin.com/jobs/view/{id} URL (including country subdomains and ?currentJobId=) returns this rendering instead of the sign-in wall.

### get_unifi_manual(url, format?)

Download a Ubiquiti UniFi installation guide (`ui.com/qig/<slug>`) as a readable document. Ubiquiti publishes no PDF for current products and draws every word of these guides as vector artwork, so a guide cannot be read as text — this rebuilds its pages and writes them to disk. `format`: `pdf` (default, one combined vector file), `png` (one image per page, viewable by a vision-capable client), or `svg`. Files land under the server's data directory. For a device's specs or price, `fetch()` its store or techspecs.ui.com page instead.

### search_eightfold_jobs(employer, title?, location?, strict_title?, include_remote?, sort?, limit?)

Search a career site hosted by Eightfold AI — `microsoft`, `netflix`, `paypal`, or any Eightfold tenant by board URL. Handles both Eightfold API generations transparently. Filter by job title and location; the tenant id is read live from the board, so a tenant fetchaller has never seen works from its URL alone. Returns title, location, department, work type, posted date, req ID, and a posting URL. Use `fetch()` on a posting URL for the full description.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| employer | string | required | "microsoft", "netflix", "paypal", or an Eightfold board URL |
| title | string | — | Job title, e.g. "software engineer" |
| location | string | — | City or country as the board spells it, e.g. "Vancouver, Canada" |
| strict_title | boolean | true | Require the title words to appear in the posting's own title |
| include_remote | boolean | true | Include remote postings in a location search |
| sort | string | relevance | relevance, recent |
| limit | integer | 25 | Jobs to return (max 100) |

### search_workday_jobs(employer, title?, location?, strict_title?, limit?)

Search any Workday board (`*.myworkdayjobs.com`) by job title and location — `adobe`, `nvidia`, `salesforce`, `autodesk`, `crowdstrike`, `servicetitan`, `motorolasolutions`, `mastercard`, or any tenant by board URL. Resolves the tenant's own location facet whatever it is named (tenants variously call it `locationCountry`, `locationHierarchy1`, or a custom field), and filters the title client-side because Workday's `searchText` silently drops real matches on some tenants.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| employer | string | required | Alias or board URL (e.g. https://acme.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/External) |
| title | string | — | Job title, e.g. "product designer" |
| location | string | — | City, region, or country; real facet values are listed when nothing matches |
| strict_title | boolean | true | Require the title words to appear in the posting's own title |
| limit | integer | 25 | Jobs to return (max 100) |

### search_oracle_jobs(employer, title?, location?, strict_title?, strict_location?, limit?)

Search a career site running on Oracle Recruiting Cloud (Oracle Fusion) — `oracle`, `uber`, or any ORC tenant by careers URL or Fusion host. Returns full posting text, location, department, and job family. The board filters by country but ignores city names, so a city is matched against each posting here.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| employer | string | required | "oracle", "uber", a careers URL, or a Fusion host |
| title | string | — | Job title, e.g. "product designer" |
| location | string | — | City and/or country, e.g. "Toronto, Canada" |
| strict_title | boolean | true | Require the title words to appear in the posting's own title |
| strict_location | boolean | true | Require the posting's own location to match |
| limit | integer | 25 | Jobs to return (max 200) |

### search_amazon_jobs(title?, location?, country?, job_category?, strict_title?, strict_location?, sort?, limit?)

Search amazon.jobs by title, location, and job category. Amazon publishes pay bands inline where local law requires it (including Canada), surfaced as a Pay field. Its own search is fuzzy in both dimensions — a "product designer" query returns engineering reqs, and a city query returns the surrounding radius — so both are re-applied against each posting. At least one of title, location, or job_category is required.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| title | string | — | Job title, e.g. "software engineer" |
| location | string | — | City or country; resolved to Amazon's exact location value automatically |
| country | string | — | ISO alpha-3 or country name; inferred from location when omitted |
| job_category | string | — | e.g. "Design", "Software Development" — the reliable way to find roles whose titles vary |
| strict_title | boolean | true | Require the title words to appear in the posting's own title |
| strict_location | boolean | true | Require the posting's own location to match, not just Amazon's radius |
| sort | string | relevant | relevant, recent |
| limit | integer | 25 | Jobs to return (max 100) |

### search_google_jobs(title, location?, strict_title?, strict_location?, remote_only?, sort?, limit?)

Search Google's own careers board by title and location. Google's free-text matching is very loose — a "product designer" search in Canada reports 38 matches of which two have a matching title — so each posting's own title and location are re-checked and both counts are reported separately.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| title | string | required | Job title, e.g. "product designer" |
| location | string | — | Country, or a fully qualified city ("Waterloo, ON, Canada" — a bare "Waterloo" resolves to Belgium) |
| strict_title | boolean | true | Require the title words to appear in the posting's own title |
| strict_location | boolean | true | Require the posting's own location to match; Google's city filter is radius-based |
| remote_only | boolean | false | Only remote-eligible postings |
| sort | string | relevance | relevance, date |
| limit | integer | 25 | Jobs to return (max 100) |

### search_apple_jobs(title, location?, locale?, strict_title?, limit?)

Search jobs.apple.com by title and location. A place name is resolved to Apple's own location code automatically. Returns title, location, team, posted date, req ID, and a posting URL.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| title | string | required | Job title, e.g. "machine learning engineer" |
| location | string | — | City or country, e.g. "Toronto", "Vancouver", "Canada" |
| locale | string | en-ca | Storefront locale; sets the country scope (en-ca, en-us, ...) |
| strict_title | boolean | true | Require the title words to appear in the posting's own title |
| limit | integer | 25 | Jobs to return (max 100) |

### search_gojobs(title?, location?, job_category?, career_level?, min_salary?, strict_title?, limit?)

Search gojobs.gov.on.ca, the Ontario Public Service careers board. The board has no keyword search of its own — its only text input is an exact Job ID — so `title` is matched against each posting's own title here. Region, city, job category, career level and minimum salary are real board filters. "Ontario" and "Canada" cover the whole board and are treated as no filter. At least one filter is required: an unfiltered listing is a dozen sequential postbacks. Returns title, organization, location, salary, closing date, Job ID, and a posting URL.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| title | string | — | Job title, e.g. "policy advisor" |
| location | string | — | Ontario city or region, e.g. "Toronto", "Thunder Bay", "North" |
| job_category | string | — | OPS category, e.g. "Information Technology" |
| career_level | string | — | Student, Entry level, Experienced, Management, Executive |
| min_salary | string | — | Minimum annual salary step, e.g. "70000" |
| strict_title | boolean | true | Require the title words to appear in the posting's own title |
| limit | integer | 25 | Jobs to return (max 100) |

### get_gojobs_job(job_id)

Full detail for one Ontario Public Service posting. Reports the competition status separately, because a filled competition still reads "Posting status: Open".

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| job_id | string | required | Numeric Job ID, e.g. "232882" |

### search_indeed(title?, location?, radius_km?, strict_title?, strict_location?, limit?)

Search ca.indeed.com. Returns the one anonymous result page Indeed reliably serves, including title, employer, location, salary and posting date. Its deeper offsets return a sign-in wall, so narrow the query to change which postings appear. At least one of title or location is required. Use `get_indeed_job` for the full description, structured salary band and listing expiry date.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| title | string | — | Job title or keywords, e.g. "administrative assistant" |
| location | string | — | City, e.g. "St. Catharines, ON" |
| radius_km | integer | 0 | Radius in km (0 uses Indeed's default 25; max 100) |
| strict_title | boolean | true | Require the title words to appear in the posting's own title |
| strict_location | boolean | false | Require the posting's own city to match; off by default because Indeed searches a radius |
| limit | integer | 25 | Jobs to return (max 100; Indeed currently exposes about 15) |

### get_indeed_job(job_key)

Read one Indeed posting in full from its public JobPosting data, including employer, location, employment type, description, salary band, posted date and `validThrough` expiry.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| job_key | string | required | Alphanumeric key from a `?jk=` Indeed URL |

### search_jobbank(title?, location?, radius_km?, strict_title?, strict_location?, limit?)

Search jobbank.gc.ca, the federal Job Bank — the highest-volume Canadian board, with salary published on most listings. A place name is resolved to Job Bank's own numeric city id first: the board silently ignores an unresolved location and returns the whole country (64,000+) as an ordinary successful search. Job Bank searches a RADIUS around a city, so nearby towns are included by design and the radius used is always reported. Its keyword is dropped for some terms ("assistant" returns the unfiltered set), which is detected and reported rather than passed off as a match count. Returns title, employer, location, salary, workplace (on site/remote/hybrid), posted date, job number, and a clean posting URL.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| title | string | — | Job title or keywords, e.g. "truck driver" |
| location | string | — | Canadian city with province, e.g. "St. Catharines, ON" |
| radius_km | integer | 50 | Radius around the city (10-500). 10km/25km/50km give 152/424/1036 near St. Catharines |
| strict_title | boolean | true | Require the title words to appear in the posting's own title |
| strict_location | boolean | false | Require the posting's own city to match. Off by default — a radius search is the point |
| limit | integer | 25 | Jobs to return (max 100) |

### search_gcjobs(title?, location?, organization?, min_salary?, language?, exclude_various_locations?, strict_title?, limit?)

Search GC Jobs (emploisfp-psjobs.cfp-psc.gc.ca), the federal public service board — the only route to Government of Canada postings, and one a plain fetch reads as empty (a "JavaScript must be enabled" shell over zero postings; the listing is a second request). Title, location, organization, minimum salary and language are real board filters, sent as the board's own form sends them and confirmed against the page's echo of what it applied; title, location and salary are re-checked here. A city filter is loose on this board (St. Catharines returned 84, of which 73 were "Various Locations" and 6 named other provinces), so the local re-check and the "Various Locations" count are always reported. Rows come back soonest-closing first. Eligibility is not on the listing — read a posting with get_gcjobs_job before relying on it. At least one filter is required. Returns title, organization, location, language requirement, salary, closing date, poster ID, and a posting URL.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| title | string | — | Job title, e.g. "policy analyst" |
| location | string | — | Canadian city or province, e.g. "St. Catharines, ON", "Ontario". "Canada" is the whole board |
| organization | string | — | Exact organization name or abbreviation, e.g. "Canada Revenue Agency", "CRA" |
| min_salary | integer | — | Minimum annual salary in dollars, matched against the bottom of each posting's range |
| language | string | — | english, french, or bilingual (the board's own facet) |
| exclude_various_locations | boolean | false | Drop postings listed as "Various Locations" |
| strict_title | boolean | true | Require the title words to appear in the posting's own title |
| limit | integer | 25 | Jobs to return (max 100) |

### get_gcjobs_job(job_id)

Full detail for one GC Jobs posting by the numeric poster ID in its URL. Reports "Who can apply" first — many federal processes are open only to current public servants, citizens, or residents of a named area — marks a posting whose closing date has passed as closed (the board serves 2001-era postings as though live), and for the third of postings the hiring organization hosts on its own site returns the outbound URL instead of an empty record.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| job_id | string | required | Numeric poster ID from the posting URL (page1800?poster=NNNNNNN), e.g. "2432896" |
### search_meta_jobs(title, location?, remote_only?, strict_title?, limit?)

Search metacareers.com by title and office. Meta spells its offices "Vancouver, Canada" rather than "Vancouver, BC"; a place name is matched against its real office list and that list is returned when nothing matches. Returns title, locations, team, sub-team, and a posting URL.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| title | string | required | Job title, e.g. "product designer" |
| location | string | — | Office, city, or country, e.g. "Toronto", "Menlo Park", "Canada" |
| remote_only | boolean | false | Only remote postings |
| strict_title | boolean | true | Require the title words to appear in the posting's own title |
| limit | integer | 25 | Jobs to return (max 100) |

### search_uber_jobs(title, location?, strict_title?, strict_location?, limit?)

Search Uber's job board by title and location. Uber runs on Oracle Recruiting, which answers anonymously with the full posting text, so results carry title, department, team, level, location, and description.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| title | string | required | Job title, e.g. "product designer" |
| location | string | — | City and/or country, e.g. "Toronto, Canada" |
| strict_title | boolean | true | Require the title words to appear in the posting's own title |
| strict_location | boolean | true | Require the city to match the posting's own location |
| limit | integer | 25 | Jobs to return (max 100) |

### search_realtor(location, transaction?, property_type?, building_type?, min_price?, max_price?, min_beds?, min_baths?, ownership?, sort?, page?)

Search Canadian homes for sale or rent on realtor.ca with full filters. Returns listings with price, address, beds/baths, size, agent, and a realtor.ca URL. Use `fetch` on a listing URL for the full description, every property detail, and similar nearby homes.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| location | string | required | City, neighbourhood, or postal code (e.g. "Ottawa", "Orleans, Ottawa", "M5V") |
| transaction | string | sale | sale, rent |
| property_type | string | any | any, residential, condo, recreational, vacant-land, multi-family, agriculture, parking |
| building_type | string | — | house, duplex, triplex, townhouse, apartment, other |
| min_price | integer | — | Minimum price (sale) or monthly rent |
| max_price | integer | — | Maximum price (sale) or monthly rent |
| min_beds | integer | — | Minimum bedrooms |
| min_baths | integer | — | Minimum bathrooms |
| ownership | string | — | freehold, condo |
| sort | string | newest | newest, oldest, price-asc, price-desc |
| page | integer | 1 | Result page (~20 per page, up to 600 total) |

### get_aliexpress_product(product_id, timeout?)

Get AliExpress product details: price, specifications, ratings, and recent reviews.

| Param | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| product_id | string | required — Numeric product ID or full AliExpress URL |
| timeout | integer | 180 — End-to-end budget in seconds (1–180) |

### search_aliexpress(query, page?, sort?, min_price?, max_price?, timeout?)

Search AliExpress products. Returns listings with prices, ratings, and links.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| query | string | required | Search query |
| page | integer | 1 | Page number (1-indexed) |
| sort | string | default | default, orders, price_asc, price_desc |
| min_price | number | — | Minimum price filter |
| max_price | number | — | Maximum price filter |
| timeout | integer | 180 | End-to-end budget in seconds (1–300) |

### get_alibaba_product(product_id, timeout?)

Get Alibaba.com B2B product details: tiered pricing, MOQ, lead times, supplier info, specifications.

| Param | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| product_id | string | required — Numeric product ID or full Alibaba.com URL |
| timeout | integer | 180 — End-to-end budget in seconds (1–300) |

### search_alibaba(query, page?, sort?, min_price?, max_price?, timeout?)

Search Alibaba.com B2B products. Returns supplier listings with tiered pricing, MOQ, and supplier info.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| query | string | required | Search query |
| page | integer | 1 | Page number (1-indexed) |
| sort | string | default | default, price_asc, price_desc |
| min_price | number | — | Minimum price filter (USD) |
| max_price | number | — | Maximum price filter (USD) |
| timeout | integer | 180 | End-to-end budget in seconds (1–300) |

## Installation

Requires Python 3.12+ and uv.

```
git clone https://github.com/Averyy/fetchaller-mcp.git
cd fetchaller-mcp
uv sync
uv run python -m patchright install chromium
uv run python -m patchright install chrome
claude mcp add fetchaller -- uv --directory "$(pwd)" run fetchaller-mcp
```

Restart Claude Code after adding. No API keys required.

### Permissions

Add to `~/.claude/settings.json` (or `.claude/settings.local.json` for per-project):

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "mcp__fetchaller__fetch",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search",
      "mcp__fetchaller__browse_reddit",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_reddit",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_marketplace",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_realtor",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_linkedin_jobs",
      "mcp__fetchaller__get_linkedin_job",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_eightfold_jobs",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_workday_jobs",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_oracle_jobs",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_amazon_jobs",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_google_jobs",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_apple_jobs",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_gojobs",
      "mcp__fetchaller__get_gojobs_job",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_indeed",
      "mcp__fetchaller__get_indeed_job",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_jobbank",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_gcjobs",
      "mcp__fetchaller__get_gcjobs_job",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_meta_jobs",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_uber_jobs",
      "mcp__fetchaller__get_aliexpress_product",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_aliexpress",
      "mcp__fetchaller__get_alibaba_product",
      "mcp__fetchaller__search_alibaba"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Optional environment variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| MOUSER_API_KEY | Mouser Search API key (enables structured API responses for mouser.com) |
| DIGIKEY_CLIENT_ID | DigiKey API client ID (enables structured API responses for digikey.com) |
| DIGIKEY_CLIENT_SECRET | DigiKey API client secret |

- [GitHub](https://github.com/Averyy/fetchaller-mcp)
